title: Recursive call correctness
statement: Fix a natural number $E$, a four-decider Boolean-word function $\mathrm{orc}$, a Boolean word $x$, and natural numbers $s,w$. For a natural number $i$, the call property says that every configuration satisfying the invariant for $s,w,i$ admits a midpoint $M'\le 2^w$ such that the program starting at the recursive-call label reaches a configuration at the return label for the truth value of bounded reachability between its source and target at level $i$, with the midpoint register set to $M'$. This run is required to satisfy the specified guard with bound $2^{w^2}$.
hypotheses_covered: Function $\mathrm{orc}$ from four deciders and Boolean words to truth values
Every starting configuration satisfies the stated invariant
caveat: The precise operational meanings of guarded reachability and the configuration encoding are not supplied, so the final sentence can only describe their role in the declaration.
